questions.stem: The MEENAKSHI Temple is located in:
questions.explanation: Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai — dedicated to goddess Meenakshi (form of Parvati) and Sundareshwar (Shiva). Dravidian style, 14 gopurams (gateway towers), currently rebuilt by the Pandyas and Nayaks. A shortlisted 'New 7 Wonders' nominee. Tamil Nadu.

questions.stem: Match the TEMPLE with its LOCATION. A. Brihadeshwara (Rajarajeshwara) Temple.  B. Somnath.  C. Jagannath Temple.  D. Sabarimala. List-II: 1. Thanjavur (TN).  2. Gujarat.  3. Puri (Odisha).  4. Kerala.
questions.explanation: Brihadeshwara (Thanjavur, TN) — built by Raja Raja Chola I, 1010 CE, UNESCO WHS. Somnath (Veraval, Gujarat) — first among Shiva's 12 Jyotirlingas. Jagannath Temple (Puri, Odisha) — Rath Yatra. Sabarimala (Kerala, Western Ghats) — Ayyappa.

questions.explanation: Tirumala Venkateswara Temple on Tirumala Hill, Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh — one of the world's richest temples, managed by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD). Dedicated to Lord Venkateswara (Vishnu).

questions.stem: The 'CHAR DHAM' pilgrimage circuit consists of:
questions.explanation: Char Dham (as defined by Adi Shankaracharya, 8th century) — Badrinath (North, Uttarakhand, Vishnu), Dwarka (West, Gujarat, Krishna), Puri (East, Odisha, Jagannath), Rameswaram (South, TN, Shiva). The 'Chota Char Dham' in Uttarakhand is a separate regional pilgrimage circuit (Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath).

questions.stem: The LINGARAJA Temple is in which city?
questions.explanation: Lingaraja Temple — Bhubaneswar, Odisha, 11th century Somavamshi dynasty. Dedicated to Harihara (combined Shiva-Vishnu form). Classic example of Kalinga / Odia temple architecture. Bhubaneswar is called the 'Temple City of India'.

questions.stem: The KHAJURAHO Group of Monuments, famous for erotic sculptures, was built by the:
questions.explanation: Khajuraho (MP) — originally 85 temples, 25 surviving (Hindu + Jain). Built by the Chandela dynasty of Bundelkhand c. 950-1050 CE. Kandariya Mahadeva is the largest. UNESCO WHS 1986. Nagara style. 9th-11th centuries.

questions.stem: The GOLDEN TEMPLE (Harmandir Sahib) at Amritsar was built by:
questions.explanation: Foundation laid by Guru Ram Das (4th Sikh Guru); construction completed by Guru Arjan Dev (5th Guru, 1589-1604). Guru Arjan Dev installed the Adi Granth there in 1604. Maharaja Ranjit Singh later added the gold plating (1830) that gives it the 'Golden Temple' name. 5th Sikh Guru.
